failure_ledger.disposition: Verified the bearer was revoked, stopped only the owned Hub process, deleted the exact empty file, issued one fresh invitation successfully, restarted the same store and consumed that invitation once. No claim or invitation was ambiguously retried.

failure_ledger.disposition: No runtime action or credential was repeated. The controller selected the bound observed vehicle from the private scenario and confirmed its recovered value after the already-completed restart.

failure_ledger.disposition: The payload already redacted the values. The check was corrected to reject all known private values and identity/location/cursor/raw structures; the same read-only diagnostics endpoint then passed.

failure_ledger.failure: The first private-root deletion ran as the guest owner and could not remove root-owned Home Assistant files.
failure_ledger.disposition: Container and Hub were already stopped. The same exact validated non-symlink root was deleted with sudo; no other path was touched.

failure_ledger.failure: The disposable Container selected the fixture-only CA file through SSL_CERT_FILE, so an unrelated Home Assistant alerts request could not validate its public certificate.
failure_ledger.disposition: The Teslatlas lane used normal certificate validation and passed its explicit system-trust rejection/private-CA trust checks. Unrelated outbound integration connectivity is not accepted by this isolated session; production operators should use a system-plus-private trust bundle when other HTTPS integrations need it.
